blog-oxidpanel-meta-description: OxidPanel is my self-built dashboard for my home server: system stats, a news aggregator and a media library with HLS streaming, built with FastAPI and Vue 3.
blog-oxidpanel-heading: OxidPanel: Dashboard for My Home Server
blog-oxidpanel-intro: OxidPanel is my self-built dashboard for my home server. It brings system monitoring, a news aggregator and a media library together in one interface.
blog-oxidpanel-screenshot-text: An excerpt of the start page: live system values, weather and the news globe.
blog-oxidpanel-module-stats: System monitoring: Live values for CPU (total and per core), memory, temperatures, load, disks, and network throughput, plus the busiest processes, history charts, and a weather tile. The view refreshes itself and pauses while the tab is hidden.
blog-oxidpanel-module-news: News: News and IT security reports from several sources, filterable by custom keywords. A globe shows where the reports come from.
blog-oxidpanel-module-media: Media: Movie and TV show library with streaming right in the browser, favorites, recently watched, and saved progress. Also usable by keyboard or TV remote.
blog-oxidpanel-tech-text: Backend in Python with FastAPI, frontend as a Vue 3 SPA with TypeScript and Vite, served directly by FastAPI. The news lives in SQLite, a scheduler in the same process keeps it current, and FFmpeg converts the videos. Everything is built in a multi-stage Docker build: one stage builds the frontend, the second serves it all. All persistent data lives in a single folder, which keeps backups simple.
blog-oxidpanel-conclusion-text: OxidPanel is a hands-on project in which I build frontend, backend, background processes, and operations myself from start to finish, from data storage and scheduled jobs to adaptive streaming.
blog-oxidpanel-news-text: Reports come from Tagesschau, IT security feeds, the CISA list of actively exploited vulnerabilities, CVE reports from NVD and GitHub, and several subreddits. Once a day a full refresh runs in the background. On top of that, the panel reloads individual feeds on demand, at most every 30 minutes.
blog-oxidpanel-news-list-1: Duplicate reports are detected by URL, even across sources
blog-oxidpanel-news-list-2: Custom keywords are matched against titles and excerpts automatically
blog-oxidpanel-news-list-3: Location detection via NLP (spaCy, German and English) for the news globe
blog-oxidpanel-news-list-4: Missing preview images are filled in from Open Graph data
blog-oxidpanel-news-list-5: Reports older than four days are cleaned up automatically
blog-oxidpanel-streaming-text: Videos are converted to HLS with FFmpeg the first time they are played, in up to three quality levels (360p, 720p, 1080p). The lowest level is built first, so the video already plays while the higher ones are still being encoded. Nothing is ever upscaled: a 720p movie gets no 1080p level. Finished conversions go into a cache that renews itself automatically when the process changes.
blog-oxidpanel-challenges-text: Reddit allows only about one request per minute without login. That is why the panel fetches the subreddits one after another with a pause instead of in parallel. The backend also deliberately runs with a single worker: the scheduler, conversion jobs, and network measurement keep their state in memory, and multiple workers would start jobs twice.
